answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled job is proven fraudulent by independent validators. Sybils do not gain influence merely by multiplying identities: each new account needs its own capital, and coordinated cheating risks losing it. The rule cannot stop every attack, but it makes identity creation costly and ties fraud to a measurable loss. A river of cheap accounts may look like an oasis, yet each must put real collateral beneath its willow-thin claim.
